text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000001 bills 99215 far above its risk-adjusted expectation, mostly on low-complexity patients, but every returned 99215 chart documents high MDM, so the evidence conflicts.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern points toward upcoding. The 99215 share is elevated in every complexity stratum, not just among sicker patients, and most 99215s fall on patients with 0–1 chronic conditions. The sample includes visits coded for back pain, abdominal pain, UTI or follow-up (for example C0000202, C0000468, C0000713, C0000872). Against that, none of the 19 documented 99215 claims was documented below the billed level, which on its face supports the coding; C0001996, a one-condition patient, is documented at high MDM. The notes themselves are the open question. The problems signal fires on 60% of returned notes (examples C0000189, C0000222, C0000251), and the time-repeat signal on some. Combined with the weak data-without-lab signal (2 of 34), this raises the possibility that notes are written to match the billed level rather than the visit, and it is not proof of that. Records cover only a small share of claims, so a reviewer should first examine the flagged problem-list notes against the low-complexity 99215 claims. A targeted chart request for those low-complexity 99215s, such as C0000202 and C0000851, would show whether the documented problems and MDM are clinically plausible for these diagnoses."}
